raw_response:
My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for three generations. The soil here is decent — flat North China Plain land. I have about 10 mu registered to my household. My son works in Shijiazhuang now, so it's mostly just me and my wife.

I will grow what I always grow: **winter wheat followed by summer maize** on 9 mu. That rotation is just how farming works here. The government gives grain subsidies for both. The seed station in town stocks Jimai 22 for wheat — I'll buy that, same as last year. For maize I'll get Xianyu 335 hybrid seed, the dealer in town always has it.

For fertilizer, I apply the same way my neighbor Old Wang does — compound base fertilizer before planting, then urea as topdress at jointing for wheat, and one split application for the maize. I don't bother with soil testing. I know from experience roughly what the field needs.

Water is the big worry. The well depth has been dropping every few years. I'll do 4 irrigation runs for wheat — sowing water, winter water, jointing, and heading — because skipping any of those kills the yield. For maize, summer rains help, so 2 irrigations should do it.

My back is not what it was. I hire the village tractor service for rotary tillage before wheat planting. After wheat harvest in June, I go straight to direct seeding maize — saves time and diesel.

I keep 1 mu for a kitchen vegetable plot — cabbage, garlic, some peppers — but that's just for the family and I won't track it formally.
